title: Something Borrowed
novel:
It was finally here — Marshall and Lily's [[wedding|wedding]] day. The [[venue|venue]] was a beautiful [[garden|garden]] overlooking a [[lake|lake]]. The flowers were [[perfect|perfect]]. The weather was [[perfect|perfect]]. Everything was perfect... until it was not.

First, Lily's [[veil|veil]] [[blew|blow]] into the lake. Then the [[pianist|pianist]] turned out to be a [[harpist|harpist]] — and she only knew one song: the theme from "[[Titanic|Titanic]]." Then the [[caterer|cater]] served the wrong meal: [[vegan|vegan]] [[lasagna|lasagna]] instead of the [[steak|steak]] Marshall had been [[dreaming|dream]] about for months.

But the biggest disaster was yet to come. The [[officiant|officiant]] was stuck in [[traffic|traffic]] on the [[George Washington Bridge|George Washington Bridge]]. Without an officiant, there could be no wedding.

"I can do it," Barney said suddenly. "I got [[ordained|ordain]] online last month as a backup."

"Why would you get ordained?" Ted asked.

"Because I wanted to be able to say 'by the power [[vested|vest]] in me,'" Barney said. "It sounds awesome."

They had no choice. As the sun [[dipped|dip]] behind the trees, Barney stood before Marshall and Lily in a white robe he had [[borrowed|borrow]] from a hotel [[spa|spa]]. He looked at his notes, then [[looked up|look up]] with tears in his eyes — real tears, which nobody had ever seen before.

"Marshall Eriksen and Lily Aldrin," he began, his voice [[shaking|shake]], "I have watched you two for years, and I have never believed in love. Until today."

The ceremony was not what anyone had [[pictured|picture]]. It was messy, it was [[improvised|improvise]], and it was the most beautiful thing any of them had ever witnessed.

wedding.en: a ceremony where two people get married

venue.en: the place where an event happens

garden.en: an area of land where flowers and plants grow

lake.en: a large area of water surrounded by land

veil.en: a thin piece of cloth a bride wears over her face

blow.en: (of wind) to move; to be moved by the wind

pianist.en: a person who plays the piano

harpist.en: a person who plays the harp

Titanic.en: the famous ship that sank in 1912; a 1997 film about it

caterer.en: a person or company that provides food for events

vegan.en: containing no animal products like meat, milk, or eggs

officiant.en: a person who performs a ceremony, especially a wedding

traffic.en: all the vehicles on a road; congestion when there are too many

ordain.en: to officially make someone a priest or minister

vest.en: to give someone the official right or power to do something

dip.en: to go down, especially below the horizon

borrow.en: to take something from someone with their permission, planning to return it

spa.en: a place where you can get beauty and health treatments

look up.en: to raise your eyes to look at something above you

improvised.en: done without preparation, using what is available

dream about.en: to think about something you wish would happen

George Washington Bridge.en: a famous bridge connecting New York and New Jersey
